newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 29.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:

* The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 4.61 points at 6,656.08 on profit-taking after blue chip stocks staged a blistering rally Tuesday. The blue-chip index has now fallen in five straight sessions, the first time it has done so since last June.
* Indonesia said on Tuesday it needs $15.7 billion in foreign aid to finance a total of 648 government-proposed projects this year.
* Indonesia said on Tuesday it was investigating dumping charges by the European Union over the country's unbleached cotton fabrics products.

* On Tuesday, the Jakarta composite index closed up 4.99 points, or 0.73 percent at 689.97 points after touching a new high of 691.49 points on the back of institutional buying in certain heavyweights, brokers said.
* On Wednesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,370.50/71.50 in early trading against the opening of 2,371.75/72.25.

* Cement maker Semen Cibinong on news it had teamed up with The Union of Myanmar Economic Holding Ltd to establish two cement plants in Myanmar. Total investment is expected to be $220 million and the plants will have a combined capacity of one million tonnes per year.
* Tin miner PT Tambang Timah on news the firm will soon develop a gold mine on a 41,000-hectare site in Natal, South Tapanuli in North Sumatera.

* Telecommunications firm PT Telkom on reports the government expected the company to invest around 4.3 trillion rupiah in the 1997 fiscal year starting April 1, compared with 4.5 trillion rupiah in fiscal 1996.

* Well-diversified Bakrie & Brothers on continued speculation the firm might sell its stake in Freeport Indonesia, which operates one of the world's largest gold and copper mines in Irian Jaya. The company said on Tuesday that no decision has been made on the matter.

* Indonesia's cement giant PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa on news it planned to use proceeds from the sale of its Bogasari Flour Mill to subscribe to an expected rights issue by its subsidiary PT Indofood Sukses Makmur. Indocement sold its stake in Bogasari for 1.86 trillion rupiah to Indofood last June.
* Retailer Matahari Putra Prima MPPI.JK on news that a Matahari department store was damaged when fire swept through a shopping complex in central Jakarta on Monday.
* Jakarta International Hotels and Development on reports its unit had secured a $232.7 million loan to finance a property project in Jakarta.
* Sierad Produce on announcement it had opened a 400-seat restaurant in China and market talk of possible link up with a Malaysian firm.
* Bimantara on news it was expected to sell its stake in tyre firm PT Intirub.
